output.query: anti-Hu paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis diagnosis and tumour screening

results.key_finding: Brainstem encephalitis is a high-risk clinical phenotype and anti-Hu a high-risk antibody (cancer association above 70%, mostly small-cell lung cancer). The PNS-Care score combines phenotype, antibody and cancer; definite PNS requires a cancer to be found. Inflammatory CSF and MRI findings support but are not required. When the initial tumour screen with CT is negative, FDG-PET is the next study.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm 78 bpm with normal intervals and no conduction disease
action_criteria.label: 12-lead ECG immediately
action_criteria.rationale: The 12-lead ECG is the first test after transient loss of consciousness (ESC 2018); a normal tracing with normal conduction argues against intrinsic conduction disease and points to an extrinsic cause of the sleep-related pauses.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Supine 138/82 mmHg, HR 78; standing 3 min 134/85 mmHg, HR 84: no orthostatic hypotension
action_criteria.label: Orthostatic blood pressure by active standing (supine, then 1 and 3 minutes standing)
action_criteria.rationale: Orthostatic blood pressure on active standing is part of the initial evaluation of every transient loss of consciousness (ESC 2018 Class I); it tests orthostatic hypotension, the competing cause, before a cardiac cause is accepted.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sleep-only sinus arrests up to 12.8 s, each preceded by prolonged absent respiration and desaturation
action_criteria.label: Inpatient telemetry with respiration and oximetry (Holter accepted)
action_criteria.rationale: Apnoeic unresponsiveness with asystole during sleep is high risk: immediate in-hospital monitoring is Class I (ESC 2018), and the sequence apnoea, desaturation, bradycardia, arrest shows the pauses are secondary to respiration.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: LVEF 55%, normal wall thickness and RV, mildly dilated LA: no structural substrate for the events
action_criteria.label: Echocardiogram to exclude structural heart disease
action_criteria.rationale: Echocardiography excludes structural heart disease as the substrate of the bradycardia and asystole (ESC 2018) and documents left ventricular function, which bears on heart-failure-related central apnoea.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Dorsal medullary T2/FLAIR hyperintensity without restricted diffusion, faint enhancement (rhombencephalitis)
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI (with contrast) for a brainstem lesion
action_criteria.rationale: Brain MRI is Class III in uncomplicated syncope but indicated here (ESC 2018): new bulbar signs (dysphagia, reduced gag) with central apnoea point to the medullary respiratory centres.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Severe central sleep apnoea (central apnoea index 54/h) with sinus pauses after prolonged central apnoeas
action_criteria.label: Attended overnight polysomnography
action_criteria.rationale: Polysomnography separates central from obstructive apnoea and shows the apnoea preceding each pause; it decides between ventilatory treatment of a central drive failure and CPAP for OSA.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) positive at high titre, other onconeural antibodies negative
action_criteria.label: Paraneoplastic antibody panel (onconeural antibodies)
action_criteria.rationale: Brainstem encephalitis in a 71-year-old former heavy smoker is a high-risk paraneoplastic phenotype; onconeural antibodies confirm the syndrome and direct the tumour search (Graus 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3.4 cm subcarinal mediastinal mass with subcarinal and right paratracheal lymphadenopathy
action_criteria.label: Tumour search for anti-Hu paraneoplastic syndrome: contrast CT of the chest
action_criteria.rationale: A high-risk antibody with a high-risk phenotype requires a tumour search, starting with contrast CT of the chest in a former smoker (Graus 2021); the tumour determines both the diagnosis and the treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lymphocytic pleocytosis, raised protein and CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for inflammatory CSF (paraneoplastic work-up)
action_criteria.rationale: Inflammatory CSF supports an immune-mediated encephalitis and excludes infection and leptomeningeal malignancy, but is not required once the antibody and MRI are diagnostic (Graus 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No respiratory depressant on the list; steroid with aspirin needs gastroprotection

action_criteria.rationale: His list contains no sedative or opioid, so the review does not change the diagnosis; it informs safe immunotherapy (gastroprotection with aspirin, glucose monitoring).

action_criteria.rationale: Literature lookup is optional; the decision rests on the monitoring, polysomnography, MRI, antibody and CT results already obtained.

required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored bed (high dependency) with continuous ECG, oximetry and capnography during sleep

general.query: syncope initial evaluation and risk stratification

results.key_finding: Initial evaluation comprises history, physical examination including supine and standing blood pressure, and a 12-lead ECG. High-risk features (syncope during exertion or supine, palpitations before the event, known structural or coronary disease, family history of sudden death under 40, high-risk ECG findings) call for early in-hospital evaluation with immediate ECG monitoring. Echocardiography is indicated when structural heart disease is known or suspected; EEG, brain imaging and routine laboratory panels are not recommended without a specific indication.
results.title: 2018 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope (Brignole M et al., Eur Heart J 2018;39:1883-1948)

results.key_finding: Risk stratification at the initial evaluation separates patients needing in-hospital monitoring and cardiac testing from those suitable for outpatient evaluation; targeted rather than routine blood testing is advised.
results.title: 2017 ACC/AHA/HRS Guideline for the evaluation and management of patients with syncope (Shen WK et al.)

general.summary: Guidelines base syncope work-up on the initial evaluation (history, examination, orthostatic BP, 12-lead ECG) and risk stratification; high-risk patients receive in-hospital ECG monitoring and targeted cardiac testing.

metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: resting ECG is normal, creating initial diagnostic uncertainty. Incidental subclinical hypothyroidism (elevated TSH) is a red herring. The critical clue of hypercapnia on ABG and the sleep-exclusive nature of events requires the agent to look beyond primary cardiac and epileptic etiologies toward a brainstem respiratory center pathology. The mediastinal mass and paraneoplastic antibodies are discoverable through appropriate follow-up testing.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Mimic case: 7 required actions (ECG, monitoring, TTE, brain MRI, polysomnography, onconeural antibodies, chest CT); brain MRI is required; the dominant red herring is the OSA anchor; cardiac, sleep and neurological data must be integrated.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Takeshi Yamamoto is a 71-year-old retired teacher with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia who is brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive in bed by his wife early this morning. She reports waking around 3 AM to find her husband apneic and cyanotic, not responding to vigorous shaking. She called emergency services. Paramedics arrived within 8 minutes and found him apnoeic and cyanotic with a faint, slow pulse; the monitor showed marked sinus bradycardia progressing to asystole lasting several seconds. With bag-mask ventilation the rhythm returned to sinus within seconds, he resumed spontaneous breathing within about 2 minutes, and he was rousable on arrival in the emergency department and fully oriented within the hour. He reports no memory of the event and states he went to sleep feeling well at approximately 10 PM. His wife notes that she has observed loud snoring and occasional gasping during his sleep over the past several weeks, which she attributed to possible sleep apnea. She also reports that approximately three weeks ago, a similar but less dramatic event occurred: she found him deeply unresponsive during sleep with blue-tinged lips, and he spontaneously recovered after she sat him upright and opened a window. He did not seek medical attention for that episode. Over the past month, the patient has noticed progressive difficulty swallowing, initially with solid foods and more recently with liquids, occasionally coughing during meals. He has also experienced increasing fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance over the past two months. He denies any syncopal episodes while awake, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, headaches, visual changes, limb weakness, numbness, or tingling. He has not had any fever, weight loss, or night sweats. There is no history of epilepsy or seizures, and the episodes have exclusively occurred during sleep.
